compatibility_notes: Four original native science page families. Shared-source image views require the AI11 host crop schema. Profiles and references are data, never permissions or human proof approvals.

design_profile.name: Science editorial / الاكتشاف المصور
typography: Live editable Tahoma Arabic and English in separate frames. Arabic without optional harakat; preserve spelling hamza.
Keep authored font sizes; short slot copy must fit readable child-facing frames.
layout: User-accepted green wave header, yellow accent, white unit badge, exact 15 mm safe margins.
Purposeful variation: vocabulary, paired observation and sequencing vs wide scene, choosing and experiment. Never repeat the same family on adjacent pages in this trial.
All captions, activity numbers, instructions, arrows, footer and card geometry are native editable objects.
Pages 3 and 4 use plant-parts/rubbing then seed investigation/journal. Preserve completed pages. Drawing and connection areas remain blank for the learner; no repeated vocabulary grid.
pedagogy: Age 5–6: notice, name, talk with a partner, sequence; then predict and investigate with a teacher.
Do not imply a plant grows in minutes; observe over several days. No unsupported educational certification.
Adult supervises soaked-bean and cotton activity. No tasting seeds or unattended water. Observe over days; do not promise a fixed germination date.
illustration: Original full-colour warm painted textbook art: precise soft shading, lively original children, purposeful actions, realistic objects and clear bean plant anatomy. Natural age 5–6 proportions, detailed gouache rendering. No publisher characters, logos, copied artwork, chibi proportions or plastic 3D look.

Recurring original pair: girl with straight dark-brown chin-length hair, orange pinafore over cream shirt; boy with short curly black hair, teal shirt. Keep faces, hair, clothes consistent. Warm cream classroom, terracotta bean pot, fresh green leaves. Believable hands, contact shadows and perspective.

Each image has only the composition requested by its own slot prompt. Scene slots contain ONE continuous scene and exactly one instance of each child. Atlas slots alone use separated cells. Do not mix scene and atlas layouts; no illustration contains text.
